July 16, 2023
The claim was reported by the claimant after a side impact at an intersection. The driver is named on the policy, and
the coverage was in force at the time of the loss.
July 19, 2023
Police attended the scene and confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle that was struck. The claimant reported neck
and back pain at the scene.
August 11, 2023
I obtained the other driver's statement, which matches the claimant's description of the collision. The other driver
stated that the light had turned in the claimant's favor.
September 27, 2023
Witnesses who spoke with me gave accounts consistent with the claimant's version of how the accident happened.
Scene photographs were also reviewed and are in the file.
October 17, 2023
The damage to the claimant's vehicle is on the driver's side and lines up with the direction and force of the impact
described. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the repair inspection.
November 5, 2023
I found nothing suggesting the damage occurred before the coverage start date. The vehicle's history was checked
and shows no prior claims on this area.
December 2, 2023
The claimant was seen at an urgent care facility the same day and was diagnosed with neck and back strain.
Treatment at that stage was consistent with the kind of force involved in a side impact.
December 4, 2023
I spoke with the claimant the following week, and the account of the accident was the same as in the first report. The
claimant has given the same description in every conversation since.
December 10, 2023
The claimant's treating provider requested authorization for physical therapy over several weeks. The course of care
was typical for this injury, and the number of visits tapered as the claimant improved.
December 13, 2023
Medical records were requested from the prior treating provider. These show long-standing treatment for the same
neck and back condition before this accident, and most of the current complaints appear to relate to that earlier
condition.
January 6, 2024
I discussed the prior records with the treating provider, who agreed that the current injury is a real strain from the
crash but that the ongoing symptoms are largely the pre-existing condition. The claim is being evaluated with that
distinction in mind.

List the facts written on this page. Copy each value exactly as it is written: same spelling,
punctuation and date format. Do not add anything that is not on this page. Use "" for a missing value.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
